newsitem.title: USA: Senators urge industry to shield heating oil users.
newsitem.headline: Senators urge industry to shield heating oil users.

text.p: Northeastern and midwestern U.S. senators urged Thursday the oil industry take steps to shield consumers from heating oil price rises this winter.

The bipartisan group, which last month raised alarm about worryingly low heating oil stocks, sent a letter to executives who were invited by Energy Secretary Hazel O'Leary Friday to discuss how to prevent market problems this winter.

"We do not want the government to interfere unnecessarily in the marketplace, and we feel that the best way to avoid any intrusive actions is for the industry to act voluntarily to protect the consumers you serve," the October 17 letter said.
The 21 senators, led by Connecticut Democrats Joseph Lieberman and Christopher Dodd, blamed the low stocks on the oil industry's efforts to maintain lean inventories to cut storage costs.

They were "concerned that the practice of keeping stocks at a bare minium exacerbates the volatility of oil industry markets and ultimately leaves consumers vulnerable to dramatic swings in prices when disruptions occur," the letter said.
"If the pattern we've seen developing this year persists, it could have serious consequences not just for the individual product markets but also for our economy as a whole," it said.
O'Leary is due to meet industry executives and a Justice Department official Friday afternoon.
Energy Department officials have repeatedly said they do not want to step into the heating oil market and have no authority themselves to bar U.S. exports of heating oil.
The department last week rejected a proposal by a bank which would have involved using oil sales from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve to help keep a lid on heating oil prices.
